verification: source-read reasoning only; no application execution or runtime reproduction
title: Advertised full Bash output is created from an already-pruned tail
conditions: The execution callback delivers more than the 102400 UTF-8-byte retained-tail cap before execution settles.
Capture pruning has removed an initial prefix, progress reports truncation, and no full-output file has previously been requested.
Post-execution temporary-file creation and append succeed.
result: The returned full-output path contains the retained tail only; the discarded prefix is irrecoverable from this capture. This finding does not require the separate OS pipe-draining defect to be present.
test_scope: The inspected existing Bash spill test uses 2001 short lines, which crosses the 2000-line presentation limit but does not cross the retained-tail byte cap. It does not establish preservation beyond 100 KiB.

local_git.scope: Attribution read from local Git history only; no upstream remote was queried.

fix_requirements: Start durable spill before the first destructive tail prune and replay every earlier captured byte exactly once.
Keep later appends in order and surface persistence failures truthfully, distinguishing incomplete logs from complete logs.
Add a future source change regression with output well above the rolling cap and verify a unique prefix, middle and suffix in the full-output file. No test was run during this audit.
